Cables categorized as Uninyvin 22 to Uninyvin 12 must be protected with an outer concentric nylon sheath to prevent fluid and mechanical abrasion.

Immersed cable specimens must withstand a test voltage of 1500 Vrms for one minute between the conductor and water without suffering dielectric breakdown.

Spark testing of core insulation specifies a potential of 3 kV (rms) up to and including size 6, a core test voltage of 1500 Vrms, and a 500 V dc spark test with minimum insulation resistance requirements.
The PVC insulation compound must be tested per IS 5831:1984. Retained tensile strength and elongation at break after heat ageing must be at least 90 percent of the unaged baseline values.

Specimens must undergo a 28-day tropical exposure conditioning test (incorporating mold growth tests per Part 10 of the environmental testing code) and then survive a 1500 Vrms voltage test with minimum insulation resistance equivalent to 4.57 M ohm for 1000 m.

certification.description: Voluntary Engineering Code of Practice. Since IS 13029:1991 is an engineering guideline rather than a direct manufacturing product, it does not carry a separate mandatory BIS license or ISI certification mark. However, its recommended practices, adjustment steps, stroboscopic methods, and advance mechanism checks are universally mandated inside all national automotive assembly plants, engine testing laboratories, public transport workshops, and homologation testing agencies (such as ARAI, VRDE, or ICAT) to perform uniform diagnostic evaluations, engine tune-ups, and baseline performance adjustments. Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable to spark ignition timing parameters.
requirements: Performed when the engine is stationary (not running) by manually rotating the crankshaft to align the designated timing marks (such as BTDC / Before Top Dead Center or TDC / Top Dead Center) on the crankshaft pulley or flywheel with the engine casing pointer. The distributor housing or electronic sensor is then aligned with the rotor. Opening of contact points or sensor trigger instant is verified by connecting a high-impedance digital multimeter or a simple low-tension test lamp across the primary ignition circuit.

Evaluated with the engine running at specified idle speed (to prevent early mechanical advance influence). A stroboscopic timing light (strobe light) is connected inductively or in-series with the spark plug cable of the No. 1 cylinder. The stroboscopic flashes are projected onto the crankshaft pulley or flywheel pointer. The distributor housing is rotated (or timing tables adjusted electronically) until the rotating index is visually aligned with the stationary timing scale to meet the manufacturer's specified advance angle.

The centrifugal mechanical advance is checked by gradually increasing engine RPM while observing the progressive forward movement of the timing marks under stroboscopic light to confirm compliance with advance curves. The vacuum advance system is checked by reconnecting the vacuum line to the intake manifold/carburetor and ensuring that timing advances further at part-throttle without sticking, diaphragm leakage, or hysteresis.

Before timing checks are finalized, spark plug gaps must be measured and set. Gaps must be adjusted strictly by bending the outer ground electrode using a wire feeler gauge, keeping the center electrode undamaged, to conform to standard clearances (ranging from 0.4 mm to 1.0 mm) depending on coil capacity.

Spark plugs must be checked for proper seating per IS 1063. Flat seating plugs must use fresh gaskets and be locked into the cylinder head using calibrated torque wrenches to prevent hot gas blow-by, cylinder thread stretching, or localized hot spots that can cause pre-ignition.

Unlike safety-critical builders hardware or transport systems under mandatory QCOs, mineral fibre slabs for shipbuilding are certified on a voluntary basis. Manufacturers are eligible to apply for a BIS license to use the Standard Mark (ISI Mark) on slab wrapping or tags. However, compliance with this specification is universally required in commercial shipyards, Indian Navy, and Coast Guard procurement tenders to ensure fire safety, structural thermal efficiency, and acoustic lagging performance on flat surfaces.
requirements: Every commercial package, crate, or bundle of slabs conforming to this standard may carry the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) along with the manufacturer's registered licence number (CM/L).
Slabs must consist of glass, rock, or slag fibres impregnated with a suitable organic or inorganic resin binder.

Standard dimensions are specified as 1000 mm length x 500 mm width. Preferred thicknesses are 25, 50, 75, or 100 mm. Alternative dimensions may be supplied as mutually agreed between the purchaser and supplier.
The maximum weight of finished slabs must not exceed values defined in the code for each specified thickness (e.g. 1 kg/m² for 25 mm slabs) to manage the ship's overall deadweight.

Slabs are tested for water absorption through partial immersion. A 150 mm x 25 mm specimen is suspended vertically with its edge immersed 6 mm below the surface of tap water for 48 hours. After immersion (and careful wiping of surface water), the water absorption must not exceed the specified limit of 4 kg/m².

To prevent galvanic corrosion on contacting steel bulkheads or aluminum hulls in marine environments, the alkalinity of the mineral fibres must be low, capped at a maximum of 1 percent when tested per IS 3144.

Un-fiberized glassy particles (shot) decrease thermal efficiency. The standard limits shot content to a maximum of 5 percent by mass for particles passing a 500-micron sieve, and 15 percent by mass for a 250-micron sieve. Any individual shot particle must not exceed 5 mm in any dimension.
For fire safety on board vessels, slabs must satisfy Class 1 flammability requirements (low flame spread) when tested in accordance with IS 13286.
To provide adequate thermal barrier performance, the thermal conductivity at a mean temperature of 20°C must not exceed 0.035 W/m°C when evaluated by the guarded hot-plate method of IS 3346.

The binder resin content (impregnation ratio) must range strictly between a minimum of 5 percent and a maximum of 10 percent by mass (tested per Annex B) to maintain structural integrity of the slabs without creating excessive organic mass.

To prevent atmospheric rust, components must be nickel-chromium electroplated per IS 1068 (minimum service grade No. 1 or 2) or chemically coloured/black-phosphated. Electroplated parts must be bright and free from peeling, blisters, or bare spots.

When assembled onto a standard frame and fork, the steering head must allow completely free, zero-play rotation of the handle bars without binding. It must survive on-road dynamic durability tests without losing alignment, cracking, or showing bearing race spalling.

Under Rule 120 of the Central Motor Vehicles Rules (CMVR), 1989, all road-going vehicles manufactured or registered in India must undergo mandatory pass-by noise type-approval (homologation) testing. Compliance with IS 3028 noise limits must be certified by designated government testing agencies (such as ARAI, GARC, or ICAT) prior to commercial vehicle release. Non-conforming vehicles cannot be registered or legally operated on Indian public roads. Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable to acoustic emission parameters.
requirements: Requires a standardized open-air testing pad comprising an acceleration track and a centralized measurement zone. Two microphones must be positioned symmetrically on both sides of the vehicle's driving centerline at a distance of 7.5 m ± 0.05 m from the path axis and at a height of 1.2 m ± 0.02 m above the track surface.

The test track pavement must satisfy strict ISO 10844 acoustic criteria. Pavement residual void content is limited to <= 8%, and the surface sound absorption coefficient must not exceed 0.10. Additionally, the macrotexture depth must be greater than or equal to 0.4 mm to prevent tire rolling-noise absorption or scattering.

Acoustic measurements are sensitive to atmospheric parameters. Outdoor wind speed at microphone height must not exceed 5 m/s during test intervals to prevent wind-induced microphone distortion. Background environmental ambient noise must be at least 10 dB(A) lower than the vehicle's peak emitted sound level.

The test evaluates sound levels under worst-case acceleration. The vehicle must approach the test line at a specified speed (or engine RPM) in a selected gear, and then accelerate at wide-open-throttle (WOT) until the rear of the vehicle exits the test zone. The peak sound level recorded on the sound level meter (A-weighted, fast response) is taken as the evaluation result.

Under Part 2 modern norms (aligned with ECE R51.03), maximum limits for passenger cars are set between 72 dB(A) to 75 dB(A), while heavy commercial vehicles (N3 category) are restricted based on engine power ranges (varying from 80 dB(A) to 85 dB(A) depending on engine output and GVW limits).

At least four measurements must be conducted on each side of the vehicle for each gear configuration. The test results are considered valid only if the difference between consecutive runs on the same side does not exceed 2 dB(A). The highest mean value calculated from the loudest side constitutes the official sound level.

Pallets must be inspected on delivery when loaded. Damaged pallets must be isolated immediately and marked at diagonally opposite vertical sides of the top corners using standard Post-Office Red paint (Color No. 538 of IS : 5-1978). The isolation mark must be exactly 100 x 100 mm in size.

Merchandise must be loaded in designed patterns to optimize stability, ensuring heavier packages are placed at the bottom and the top is levelled off. Bag cargo for export must be vacuum-packed with side bag walls to provide a flat top surface and prevent loosening during transport.

Pallets must never be pushed or dragged with truck forks. The operator must raise and lower pallets carefully, avoid driving collisions, fully lower and immobilize forks before leaving the truck, and trail the load rather than pushing it.

certification.description: Voluntary Quality and Performance Specification. Certification under the BIS ISI Mark Scheme is voluntary for this standard. However, compliance with IS 8752:1978 is universally mandated by Regional Transport Offices (RTOs), vehicle type-approval laboratories (such as ARAI, GARC, and ICAT) under Rule 120 of the Central Motor Vehicles Rules (CMVR), 1989, and public logistics contracts to guarantee coupling safety, ensure roadworthiness of laden trains, and prevent tractor-trailer decoupling. Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable.
requirements: Every certified towing hook conforming to this standard may be legibly marked with the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) along with the manufacturer's registered licence number (CM/L) on the body.

Towing hooks must be either forged or cast. Forged hooks must be manufactured from Grade C30 carbon steel per IS 1875-1971 in a normalized heat-treatment condition. Cast hooks must be manufactured from Grade 2 1.5% manganese steel castings per IS 2708-1973.
The towing hook is strictly restricted to light haulage applications. The gross laden train mass (including single or multiple towed trailers) must not exceed 5 tonnes.

An efficient safety catch must be provided as shown in Fig. 1. The safety catch must lock automatically or be manually secured to prevent accidental detachment of the trailer drawbar eye from the hook during dynamic field movements.

Each towing hook must be legibly and permanently marked at an appropriate place with: a) 'TO TOW 5 TONNES GROSS' on one side of the body; and b) 'IS : 8752' on the opposite side to designate its maximum capacity and standard conformity.
All coupling jaw openings, hook curvatures, and shank dimensions must conform strictly to Fig. 1 to ensure standard clearance and seamless matching with drawbar eyes.

certification.description: Voluntary Quality and Performance Specification. Unlike mass-market commercial fasteners, high-integrity aerospace fasteners like solid nickel alloy rivets are certified on a voluntary basis under the BIS ISI Certification scheme. Manufacturers are eligible to apply for a BIS license to print the Standard Mark (ISI Mark) on bulk boxes or tags. However, compliance with this specification is universally required by State Aerospace manufacturers (such as HAL), defense research laboratories (DRDO), military aviation procurement agencies (IAF), and space organizations (ISRO) to ensure zero failure under high-vibration structural environments.
requirements: Every certified package, box, or batch of rivets conforming to this standard may carry the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) to verify quality and safety.
Alloy No. 1 rivets must possess a minimum ultimate tensile strength of 490 N/mm² or a minimum shear strength of 350 N/mm² (with tensile and shear strengths treated as alternative mechanical tests).
Alloy No. 2 rivets must possess a minimum ultimate tensile strength of 650 N/mm² or a minimum shear strength of 450 N/mm² (with tensile and shear strengths treated as alternative mechanical tests).
Alloy No. 1 rivets must be fully annealed by the rivet manufacturer prior to delivery. Delivered in an 'As manufactured' state, closed in an 'As delivered' state, and used in an 'As closed' state.
Alloy No. 2 rivets require no pre-delivery heat treatment. Delivered in an 'As manufactured' state, closed in an 'As delivered' state, and used in an 'As closed' state.

Defines nine standard nominal shank diameters (d) with strict bilateral tolerances to ensure interference-fit reliability in airframe skin holes:
a) 1.6 mm: ±0.05 mm
b) 2.4 mm: +0.06 / -0.04 mm
c) 3.2 mm: ±0.05 mm
d) 4.0 mm: ±0.06 mm
e) 4.8 mm: +0.05 / -0.07 mm
f) 5.6 mm: +0.05 / -0.07 mm
g) 6.4 mm: +0.05 / -0.07 mm
h) 8.0 mm: +0.03 / -0.10 mm
i) 9.6 mm: +0.03 / -0.10 mm

All physical identification symbols indented on the rivet head must have a controlled depth of approximately 0.2 mm to ensure the structural and fatigue resistance of the rivet head is not compromised.

Mandates a standardized nomenclature for engineering drawings, purchase orders, and stock records. Format: 'Universal Head Rivet [Diameter] x [Length] Alloy [Alloy No.] IS : 9088'. Example: 'Universal Head Rivet 8 x 10 Alloy 1 IS : 9088'.

Rivets must be packed securely as agreed between the purchaser and supplier. Each package must be legibly marked with: a) Manufacturer's name or trade-mark; b) Rivet designation; c) Quantity; and d) Particulars of the Inspector or Inspector's stamp to ensure full QA traceability.
